title: Consistent hashing with virtual nodes
prompt:
The reading app caches student progress across a pool of cache servers. The starter code picks a server with hash(key) % servers.length. Run the tests: when one server is added or removed, almost every key moves to a different server, so the whole cache goes cold at once. Replace it with a hash ring.

API: new HashRing({ vnodes = 100, hash = hash32 } = {})

  • addNode(name): place vnodes points on the ring for this server, at hash(name + '#' + i) for i = 0 .. vnodes-1.
  • removeNode(name): remove all its points.
  • getNode(key): hash the key, walk clockwise to the first point whose position is >= the key's hash, and return that point's server. If you pass the end of the ring, wrap to the first point. Return undefined if the ring is empty.

Keep the points in an array sorted by position. Binary search is nice; a linear scan also passes the tests.

tests.name: empty ring returns undefined; one node owns everything
walks clockwise and wraps around (hand-placed positions)
removing a node only moves the keys that were on it
adding a 4th node moves roughly 1/4 of keys, all to the new node
virtual nodes spread load fairly evenly
the same key always maps to the same node

hints: Store points as objects { pos, node } in one array. After addNode, sort by pos. removeNode is a filter.
In getNode, find the first point with pos >= hash(key). If none exists (the key hashes past the last point), the answer is ring[0]: that's the wrap-around.
Binary search shape: let lo = 0, hi = ring.length; while (lo < hi) { const mid = (lo + hi) >> 1; if (ring[mid].pos < h) lo = mid + 1; else hi = mid; } return ring[lo === ring.length ? 0 : lo].node;
explain:
With % N, going from 3 to 4 servers remaps about 3 out of 4 keys (a key stays only if h % 3 === h % 4). With a ring, only the keys in the arcs the new server takes over move: about 1/N. Virtual nodes (many points per server) fix the uneven arcs you get with one point per server, and let a bigger machine take more points. Dynamo, Cassandra, Riak, many memcached clients and some load balancers use this idea; Redis Cluster uses a related trick (16,384 fixed hash slots assigned to nodes).

In an interview: "I'd shard the cache by key with consistent hashing and ~100 virtual nodes per server, so adding a node moves only about 1/N of the keys and we don't get a cold-cache stampede on the database."
